questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Use technology to find the correlation coefficient r for the data (1, 9), (2, 8), (3, 8), (4, 6), (5, 5), (6, 5), (7, 3), (8, 2), to the nearest hundredth. Describe the association.
questions.prompt_markup:
Use technology to find the correlation coefficient r for the data
(1, 9), (2, 8), (3, 8), (4, 6), (5, 5), (6, 5), (7, 3), (8, 2),
to the nearest hundredth. Describe the association.
questions.correct_answer: r ≈ -0.98: a strong negative linear association.
questions.grading_note: Form required: r to the nearest hundredth and a description.

sections.skill: Use simulation to judge whether a correlation could be due to chance

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Use simulation to judge whether a correlation could be due to chance
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: In 1,000 random shufflings of the y-values, r was at least 0.9 in 2 trials. The observed r is 0.92. Is the association likely to be due to chance?
questions.prompt_markup:
In 1,000 random shufflings of the y-values, r was at least 0.9 in 2 trials. The observed r is 0.92.
Is the association likely to be due to chance?
questions.correct_answer: No. A correlation this strong happened only about 0.2% of the time by chance.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the answer and the reason.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Use simulation to judge whether a correlation could be due to chance
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: For a different data set, shuffled data gave r ≥ 0.3 in 350 of 1,000 trials, and the observed r is 0.3. What is the conclusion?
questions.prompt_markup:
For a different data set, shuffled data gave r ≥ 0.3 in 350 of 1,000 trials, and the observed r is 0.3.
What is the conclusion?
questions.correct_answer: The association could easily be due to chance (about 35%).
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent conclusion.

sections.skill: Evaluate claims based on a correlation

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Evaluate claims based on a correlation
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A news story says, "r = 0.6, so 60% of the change in sales is caused by advertising." Name two errors.
questions.prompt_markup:
A news story says, "r = 0.6, so 60% of the change in sales is caused by advertising."
Name two errors.
questions.correct_answer: r is not a percent of change (r² ≈ 0.36 describes the share of variation explained), and correlation does not show causation.
questions.grading_note: Form required: two errors.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Evaluate claims based on a correlation
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A study of 8 cities finds r = 0.7 between the number of parks and happiness scores. Why should you be cautious?
questions.prompt_markup:
A study of 8 cities finds r = 0.7 between the number of parks and happiness scores.
Why should you be cautious?
questions.correct_answer: The sample is small, the study is observational, and other variables (such as income) could explain both.
questions.grading_note: Any two valid reasons.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions

questions.prompt_markup: Which statement about r = -0.9 is correct?

choices.text: There is a strong negative linear association.
The slope of the line is -0.9.
90% of the points are on the line.
An increase in x causes y to fall.

questions.correct_answer: There is a strong negative linear association.
questions.grading_note: r measures the direction and strength of a linear association only.
